source.name: Grantitude
source.note: Compiled full-funding dataset by Grantitude. Imported entries are limited to institutions whose published coverage includes BOTH tuition and room/board. No academic benchmarks (GPA, SAT, acceptance rate) exist in the source, so none are stored here and none are inferred. Programme text is reproduced in English as published.

institutions.name: Harvard University
institutions.scholarship: Need-blind for internationals; meets 100% of need
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Restrictive Early Action · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Families earning under $100K pay nothing; under $200K, full tuition is covered. COA 2025-26 is ~$86,900.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants including internationals; aid meets 100% of demonstrated need.

institutions.name: Yale University
institutions.scholarship: Need-blind admissions; meets 100% of demonstrated need
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Restrictive Early Action · January 2 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Families earning under $75K pay nothing; under $200K will pay no tuition starting 2026-27. No loans in any aid package.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants including internationals; 100% of demonstrated need met.

institutions.name: Princeton University
institutions.scholarship: No-loan policy since 2001; grants cover full demonstrated need
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Single-Choice Early Action · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: All aid given as grants — zero loans. Families under $100K typically pay nothing.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants including internationals — one of very few US universities with this policy. Meets 100% of demonstrated need with zero loans. Families up to $150K fully covered; up to $250K pay no tuition (2025-26).

institutions.name: Brown University
institutions.scholarship: Need-blind for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 6 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans; all aid packaged as grants and work-study.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants including internationals as of Fall 2025 (Class of 2029) — Brown completed a $120M fundraising initiative to achieve this. One of ~8 US colleges need-blind for internationals.

institutions.name: University of Pennsylvania
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need once admitted
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 5 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans; grant-only aid packages. Automatic consideration upon admission.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants — financial need is considered in admissions. Once admitted, 100% of demonstrated need is met with no loans.

institutions.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
institutions.scholarship: Need-blind for all; meets 100% of demonstrated need with no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Action · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: All aid given as grants; no loans. About 90% of students receive some form of aid.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants worldwide including internationals.

institutions.name: Stanford University
institutions.scholarship: Meets 100% of demonstrated need; families under $75K pay nothing
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Restrictive Early Action · January 2 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Families earning under $75K pay nothing; under $150K, no expected tuition contribution. No loans.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for US citizens; need-aware for internationals, but meets 100% of demonstrated financial need once admitted.

institutions.name: Amherst College
institutions.scholarship: Need-blind for all worldwide; meets full need with no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 8 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans in aid packages. One of the very few colleges need-blind for all international applicants worldwide.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants worldwide; 100% of demonstrated need met.

institutions.name: Swarthmore College
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; full need met once admitted, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision · January 3 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans; grants and work-study only. Once admitted, 100% of demonstrated need is met.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants — financial need may factor into admissions. Once admitted, 100% of demonstrated need met with no loans.

institutions.name: Bowdoin College
institutions.scholarship: Need-blind for all; meets full demonstrated need, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 5 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: All aid packaged as grants and work-study; zero loans.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants including internationals (expanded in 2022); 100% of demonstrated need covered.

institutions.name: Pomona College
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need once admitted, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 6 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: ~$74,000 average grant for international students receiving aid
coverage.notes: No loans; all grants. One of the Claremont Colleges. Need-aware for international applicants.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for US citizens/permanent residents. Need-aware for international applicants — financial need considered in admissions. Aid must be declared on application. Once admitted, 100% of need met.

institutions.name: Washington and Lee University
institutions.scholarship: Johnson Scholarship — full tuition + room/board + $10,000 summer fund
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + room + board + $10,000 summer funding = $89,000+/yr
coverage.notes: Johnson Scholarship covers full tuition, room, board, and $10,000/yr for funded summer experiences. ~44 scholarships awarded per year (~10% of class). W&L is need-blind and meets 100% of need for all admitted students.

eligibility.notes: Highly competitive; apply via Johnson Scholarship essay on Common App Writing Supplement by December 1. Open to all nationalities.

institutions.name: Wesleyan University
institutions.scholarship: Freeman Asian Scholarship — full cost of attendance ($90K+) including airfare; meets full need for others
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision I · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: Freeman Scholars: $90,000+/yr full cost of attendance including annual airfare; ~11 awarded/year
coverage.notes: Freeman Asian Scholarship covers full cost of attendance including tuition, fees, room, board, supplies, and annual round-trip airfare for ~11 students/year from China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam. Auto-considered upon applying. Need-aware for non-Freeman internationals.

eligibility.notes: Freeman Asian Scholarship for citizens/permanent residents of 11 Asian countries; ~11 spots/year. Automatically considered. Non-Freeman internationals: need-aware admissions.

institutions.name: Colby College
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; full need met once admitted, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Colby Commitment: no loans in any aid package. Full need met for all admitted students.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants — financial need is a factor in admissions. Once admitted, 100% of demonstrated need is met with grants and work-study only (no loans).

institutions.name: Minerva University
institutions.scholarship: Need-based grants available; tuition ~$25,000/yr (2025-26); 80% of students receive aid
institutions.deadline: Rolling admissions — priority by March 1

coverage.annualValue: Tuition ~$25,000/yr + residential fee ~$17,400/yr = ~$44,700 COA before aid; avg grant ~$19,277
coverage.notes: Unique rotational global program. 80% of students receive need-based grants averaging ~$19,277; net price after aid ~$26,103. Tuition has risen significantly from earlier years.

eligibility.notes: Holistic admissions; no standardized test required. Students from 100+ countries attend.

institutions.name: University of Oxford
institutions.scholarship: Rhodes & Reach Oxford — full tuition + stipend
institutions.deadline: October 15, 2025 — UCAS · February 4, 2026 — Reach Oxford

coverage.notes: Reach Oxford covers tuition, college fees, living grant, and one return airfare per year.

eligibility.notes: Reach Oxford is for students from low-income countries (DAC/OECD list) with significant financial need; ~6–8 awarded annually. Must intend to return home after studies. Apply via UCAS by Oct 15; scholarship application window Jan 14–Feb 4, 2026.

institutions.name: The University of Hong Kong
institutions.scholarship: HKU Foundation Entrance Scholarship — full tuition + living
institutions.deadline: November 26 — First-round (rolling thereafter; final August 21)

coverage.annualValue: Top scholarships cover full tuition (~HKD 198,000/yr) + living allowances; 43+ scholarships available
coverage.notes: HKU offers tiered entrance scholarships automatically upon admission — no separate application required. Top scholarships cover full tuition (~HKD 198,000) + living allowances. Some scholarships are faculty-specific.

eligibility.notes: All admitted applicants automatically considered — no separate scholarship application required. Result announced with admission offer.

institutions.name: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
institutions.scholarship: Academic Scholarship — full tuition + up to HKD 60,000 annual allowance
institutions.deadline: Early round: November 20, 2025 · Main round: January 8, 2026

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition (~HKD 180,000–200,000) + allowance up to HKD 60,000/yr
coverage.notes: Academic scholarships awarded automatically upon admission — no separate application. Maximum scholarship: full tuition + HKD 60,000 allowance/yr. Strong STEM and business programs.

eligibility.notes: International students auto-considered upon admission application. Strong academics and English required.

institutions.name: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
institutions.scholarship: Admission Scholarship — up to full tuition HKD 214,000 + HKD 66,000 living allowance
institutions.deadline: Advance round: November 13, 2025 · Regular round: January 8, 2026

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition HKD ~214,000 + living allowance up to HKD 66,000 for top Admission Scholarship holders
coverage.notes: Tiered Admission Scholarships range from HKD 5,000 to full tuition + HKD 66,000 living allowance. The VC Scholarship for Excellence is a separate one-time HKD 50,000 award (8 per year, not specifically for internationals). No airfare/travel component confirmed.

eligibility.notes: Non-local applicants from all countries eligible. Awarded based on academic excellence and extra-curricular achievements.

institutions.name: The Education University of Hong Kong
institutions.scholarship: Entrance Scholarships — full tuition + accommodation for international students
institutions.deadline: January 31 — Non-local undergraduate applications

coverage.notes: Specialized education/social sciences university. Full-tuition scholarships with living allowance for top international admits. On-campus housing available separately — not always included in scholarship package.

eligibility.notes: Primarily for education and social science programs. Non-local students eligible for entrance scholarships.

institutions.name: Constructor University
institutions.scholarship: Fully funded JetBrains Foundation Scholarship for BSc Software, Data and Technology
institutions.deadline: March 10, 2026 — BSc SDT application deadline for JetBrains scholarship consideration

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + room & board + university fee + semester ticket + first-year pocket money
coverage.notes: For the BSc Software, Data and Technology program. The JetBrains Foundation scholarship covers tuition, room and board, university fee, semester ticket, and pocket money for the first year. Applicants not selected can still use regular Constructor University financing options such as academic achievement scholarships and tuition deferral.

eligibility.notes: For first-year applicants to the BSc Software, Data and Technology program. Applicants must apply to BSc SDT and register for one of the scholarship competitions; winners are invited to a JetBrains Foundation interview with technical questions in informatics and mathematics, motivation assessment, and review of academic achievements such as Olympiads, competitions, online courses, and extra classes.

institutions.name: KAIST
institutions.scholarship: Full tuition waiver + KRW 350,000/month stipend + campus housing for all international UG admits
institutions.deadline: December — International Undergraduate Admissions (for March enrollment)

coverage.notes: All international undergraduate students receive full tuition waiver + dormitory + monthly stipend as standard. No separate scholarship application needed.

eligibility.notes: Must hold non-Korean citizenship. Strong STEM background required. TOEFL 83 or IELTS 6.5 minimum. Conducted entirely in English.

institutions.name: DGIST
institutions.scholarship: Full tuition + KRW 300,000–600,000/month stipend + dormitory + arrival travel grant
institutions.deadline: January — International Undergraduate Admissions

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + dormitory + stipend + arrival travel grant (KRW 3,000,000 Americas/Europe; KRW 1,500,000 Asia)
coverage.stipendAmount: KRW 600,000/month for Americas/Europe students; KRW 300,000/month for Asian students (~$220–440/month)
coverage.notes: DGIST offers a unique undeclared interdisciplinary program for first 2 years. All international undergrads receive full scholarship. Stipend and travel grant amounts vary by region of origin.

eligibility.notes: Non-Korean citizens only. All instruction in English. Strong science/math background required. Very small cohort.

institutions.name: GIST
institutions.scholarship: Full tuition + KRW 300,000/month stipend + dormitory via GIST & Korean Govt Scholarship
institutions.deadline: October–December — Korean Govt Scholarship; January — GIST direct

coverage.notes: GIST International Student Scholarship: full tuition + dorm + monthly allowance. Korean Government Scholarship (GKS) also routes here: adds airfare + settlement allowance.

eligibility.notes: Non-Korean citizens. Science/engineering focus. Instruction in English.

institutions.name: POSTECH
institutions.scholarship: Full tuition + KRW 500,000/month stipend + dorm + Pathfinder Voucher + arrival airfare reimbursement
institutions.deadline: November — International Undergraduate Admissions (for March enrollment)

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + campus dorm + KRW 6,000,000/yr stipend + KRW 2,500,000 Pathfinder Voucher + arrival airfare reimbursement (up to KRW 2,500,000)
coverage.notes: POSTECH — top STEM university in Korea. All international undergrads receive: full tuition, dormitory, KRW 500,000/month stipend, KRW 2,500,000/yr Pathfinder Voucher for enrichment activities, and one-time arrival airfare reimbursement (up to KRW 2,500,000).

eligibility.notes: Non-Korean citizens only. Very selective. Strong STEM foundation required. English-medium instruction.

institutions.name: NYU Abu Dhabi
institutions.scholarship: Need-blind; full need covered including tuition, housing, meals, flights & personal allowance
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: Full cost of attendance ~$75,000/yr including two round-trip flights
coverage.notes: Among the world's most generous packages: full tuition + housing + meals + transportation + personal allowance + two round-trip flights home per year. Need-blind for all applicants.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants worldwide. No separate scholarship application — financial aid automatic with admission. Must submit CSS Profile.

institutions.name: MBZUAI
institutions.scholarship: Full tuition + AED 8,000/month stipend + furnished housing for all admits (graduate)
institutions.deadline: January 31 — Spring intake · May 31 — Fall intake

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + furnished housing + AED 96,000/yr stipend
coverage.notes: Graduate-level institution (MSc, PhD) in AI/ML. All admits receive full scholarship including stipend and accommodation. Note: no undergraduate degree programs currently offered.

eligibility.notes: Graduate programs only — bachelor's degree required to apply. Strong background in CS/mathematics needed.

institutions.name: King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals
institutions.scholarship: Full-ride: tuition, on-campus housing, monthly stipend, subsidized dining, 2 round-trip flights/year, on-campus medical clinic
institutions.deadline: SAT track opens annually — check apply.kfupm.edu.sa for current dates

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition (waives SR 20,000/yr baseline) + free on-campus housing + monthly stipend + subsidized dining + 2 round-trip flights/year + on-campus medical clinic + complimentary textbooks
coverage.stipendAmount: ~SAR 990/month (~$264) per current student reports; not officially published
coverage.notes: QS World #67 (2026), #1 Arab university. STEM-focused, all instruction in English. 75+ nationalities on campus; ~5–7% of undergrads international. Major feeder to Saudi Aramco.

eligibility.notes: Two tracks for international undergrads: (1) SAT track — SAT 1350+ plus KFUPM's own online math assessment; (2) ISEF Winners track — top 4 ISEF winners/year get guaranteed admission and full scholarship with no SAT required. No portfolio track. Natural sciences focus in high school required for SAT track. Maintain GPA ≥ 3.0 once enrolled. Admission decisions take 2–3 months.

institutions.name: Carnegie Mellon University in Qatar
institutions.scholarship: Need-based aid meets full demonstrated need; many students receive full ride
institutions.deadline: January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: Full cost of attendance (~$77,000/yr equivalent) for qualifying students
coverage.notes: Qatar Foundation funds the campus. Financial aid packages mirror CMU Pittsburgh and can cover full demonstrated need. CS, Business, and Information Systems programs.

eligibility.notes: Open to students from all nationalities. Same application process and admission standards as CMU Pittsburgh. CSS Profile required for aid.

institutions.name: Georgetown University in Qatar
institutions.scholarship: Need-based financial aid covering full demonstrated need; no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Action · January 10 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: Full cost of attendance for qualifying students
coverage.notes: Qatar Foundation funds the campus. Same need-blind financial aid philosophy as main campus. International Affairs and Business programs. No loans in packages.

eligibility.notes: Open worldwide. Need-blind for all applicants including internationals. CSS Profile required.

institutions.name: Northwestern University in Qatar
institutions.scholarship: Need-based aid covers full demonstrated need; no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: Full cost of attendance for demonstrated need
coverage.notes: Qatar Foundation-funded campus. Journalism and Communication programs. Same financial aid commitment as Northwestern Evanston. All aid in grants.

eligibility.notes: Open to all nationalities. Need-blind admissions. CSS Profile + FAFSA (if applicable) required.

institutions.name: National University of Singapore
institutions.scholarship: ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship — full tuition + SGD 5,800/yr allowance + housing
institutions.deadline: March 26 — ASEAN Scholarship application deadline (AY2026/2027)

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + campus housing + SGD 5,800 annual allowance
coverage.stipendAmount: SGD 5,800/year (~$4,300) living allowance + SGD 3,000/yr accommodation allowance + SGD 1,750 one-time computer allowance
coverage.notes: ASEAN Scholarship: full tuition, campus accommodation, annual living allowance, settling-in allowance. Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship also available for exceptional applicants globally.

eligibility.notes: ASEAN Scholarship for citizens of ASEAN countries. Science & Technology Scholarship open globally. Strong academic record required.

institutions.name: Nanyang Technological University
institutions.scholarship: Nanyang Scholarship — full tuition + SGD 6,500/yr allowance + campus housing
institutions.deadline: January 15 — Scholarship application deadline; March–May — Selection interviews

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + on-campus hall + SGD 6,500 annual allowance
coverage.stipendAmount: SGD 6,500/year (~$4,800) + S$2,000 one-time computer allowance + up to S$8,000 overseas travel grant
coverage.notes: Nanyang Scholarship: full tuition, hall accommodation, SGD 6,500/yr living allowance, S$2,000 computer allowance, up to S$8,000 overseas travel grant. Enrollment in NTU Honours College required. ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship also available for ASEAN nationals.

eligibility.notes: Open to internationals worldwide. ASEAN Scholarship specifically for ASEAN nationals. Strong academics required; top 5% of cohort.

institutions.name: Tsinghua University
institutions.scholarship: Chinese Government Scholarship — full tuition + CNY 2,500/month stipend + dorm
institutions.deadline: February–April — CSC applications (varies by country; embassy Type A or Tsinghua Type B)

coverage.notes: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC): full tuition, campus accommodation, monthly stipend. Tsinghua University Scholarship also available. Schwarzman Scholars is graduate-level only.

eligibility.notes: Non-Chinese citizens eligible. Apply via CSC portal or through Chinese embassies. Many programs taught in Chinese — verify language of instruction.

institutions.name: CUHK Shenzhen
institutions.scholarship: Honor Scholarship — CNY 165,000/yr; tiered entry scholarships from CNY 30,000–165,000/yr
institutions.deadline: March — International Undergraduate Admissions

coverage.annualValue: Honor Scholarship: CNY 165,000/yr; Full Tuition: CNY 140,000/yr; Half Tuition: CNY 70,000/yr; Inspirational: CNY 30,000/yr
coverage.notes: Four-tier entry scholarships automatically considered upon admission — no separate application: Honor (CNY 165,000/yr), Full Tuition (CNY 140,000/yr), Half Tuition (CNY 70,000/yr), Inspirational (CNY 30,000/yr). Honor Scholarship exceeds tuition (~CNY 140,000), effectively covering living costs. Academic Performance Scholarships (CNY 20,000–80,000/yr) available for continuing students.

eligibility.notes: Non-Chinese citizens. Programs in English. Strong academic record required.

institutions.name: HKUST (Guangzhou)
institutions.scholarship: Admission Scholarship (merit-based) + Guangdong Govt Outstanding Int'l Student Scholarship (RMB 10,000/yr)
institutions.deadline: February — International undergraduate applications

coverage.annualValue: Admission Scholarship (merit-based, amount varies) + Guangdong Govt Scholarship RMB 10,000/yr for continuing students
coverage.notes: HKUST Guangzhou awards Admission Scholarships to top international applicants — no separate application required. The 'Red Bird' name refers to the postgraduate MPhil program, not an undergraduate scholarship. Guangdong Government Outstanding International Student Scholarship (RMB 10,000/yr) available for continuing UG students. Interdisciplinary Hubs model curriculum. English-medium.

eligibility.notes: Non-Chinese citizens. English-medium. Innovative cross-disciplinary curriculum.

institutions.name: Southern University of Science and Technology
institutions.scholarship: SUSTech President Scholarship — full tuition + RMB 65,500/yr package + housing + insurance
institutions.deadline: April–May — International undergraduate applications (check infoadmin.sustech.edu.cn)

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition waiver (~RMB 30,000) + housing + insurance + RMB 65,500 total annual package (~$9,000)
coverage.notes: President Scholarship covers 100% tuition, campus dormitory, medical insurance, and a living stipend. All undergraduate programs at SUSTech are English-medium — no Chinese language required. Guangdong Government Outstanding Foreign Student Scholarship (RMB 10,000/yr) also available as supplementary award.

eligibility.notes: Non-Chinese citizens eligible. Strong STEM academic background required. All programs taught in English — IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 80 minimum (waived for native English speakers or those with prior English-medium education). Programs span physics, chemistry, biology, materials science, engineering, computer science, mathematics, and finance. Apply via infoadmin.sustech.edu.cn.

institutions.name: Hamad Bin Khalifa University
institutions.scholarship: Full tuition + QAR 5,000/month stipend + housing for graduate programs
institutions.deadline: February 1 — Graduate applications (note: primarily graduate institution)

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + campus housing + QAR 60,000/yr stipend
coverage.notes: Qatar Foundation-funded. Primarily graduate programs (MSc, PhD, professional degrees). Full scholarships for all admitted graduate students.

eligibility.notes: Mainly graduate-level. Select undergraduate programs may be available. English-medium instruction.

institutions.name: Qatar University
institutions.scholarship: International Students Scholarship — full tuition + accommodation + annual airfare + QAR 500/month stipend
institutions.deadline: October 22 — Spring intake; verify Fall 2026 deadline at qu.edu.qa

coverage.annualValue: Full tuition + on-campus housing + annual round-trip airfare + QAR 500/month stipend + textbook exemption
coverage.notes: Full scholarship package: tuition, shared on-campus housing, annual round-trip airfare, QAR 500/month stipend, and textbook exemption. ~500 international scholarship slots. Minimum 95% high school average typically required. Strong engineering and sciences programs.

eligibility.notes: Non-Qatari nationals eligible. Minimum 95% high school average required for scholarship. Some programs in Arabic only; verify English-medium options.

institutions.name: University of British Columbia
institutions.scholarship: Karen McKellin International Leader of Tomorrow Award — full demonstrated need
institutions.deadline: November 15 — International Scholars Program application; December 1 — UBC admission application

coverage.annualValue: Full cost of attendance including tuition, housing, meals, books, and travel
coverage.notes: Karen McKellin Award is highly competitive (about 15–20 awarded/year worldwide). Covers full demonstrated financial need. Separate scholarship application required.

eligibility.notes: For students outside Canada. Exceptional academic achievement and leadership required. Separate application due December 1.

institutions.name: University of Toronto
institutions.scholarship: Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship — full tuition + books + residence + incidentals
institutions.deadline: October 10 — School nomination deadline · November 7 — Student application deadline

coverage.annualValue: Full cost of attendance ~CAD $70,000/yr (tuition + residence + books + incidentals)
coverage.notes: Lester B. Pearson Scholarship: full tuition, residence, meal plan, and books for 4 years. About 37 awarded per year from 150+ countries. Must be nominated by your high school.

eligibility.notes: Must be nominated by your secondary school. For international students (non-Canadian). Extraordinary academic achievement and demonstrated impact required.

institutions.name: Barnard College
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need once admitted, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision I · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans in any aid package. Meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for all admitted students. Need-aware for international first-year applicants.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. Aid cannot be applied for after admission. Once admitted, 100% of demonstrated need is met with no loans.

institutions.name: Bates College
institutions.scholarship: Meets full demonstrated need; no-loan policy for qualifying students
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans for students with family income under $60K. Need-aware for internationals but strong aid commitment.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. Strong academic and extracurricular profile expected.

institutions.name: Bryn Mawr College
institutions.scholarship: Meets full demonstrated need for all admitted students; no loans
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 15 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Meets full demonstrated need. Aid packages for international students may include grants, loans, and campus employment — 'no loans' is not guaranteed for internationals. Women's college with strong STEM and humanities programs.

eligibility.notes: Need-sensitive (need-aware) for internationals. Aid must be requested at time of application — no changes allowed later. Aid packages may include loans for internationals.

institutions.name: California Institute of Technology
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need once admitted
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Action · January 3 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Meets 100% of demonstrated need; packages include grants, scholarships, work-study, and loans. Need-blind for domestic students; need-aware for international applicants due to limited international aid funding.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. Aid must be applied for at time of admission application. Science and engineering focused.

institutions.name: Carleton College
institutions.scholarship: Meets 100% of demonstrated need for all admitted students; no loans
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 15 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans in aid packages. Carleton meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted students.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for internationals; strong aid commitment once admitted.

institutions.name: Claremont McKenna College
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need once admitted, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision I · January 10 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans. One of the Claremont Colleges. Need-aware for international applicants — financial need may affect admission. Once admitted, 100% of need met.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. CMC uses its own International Student Financial Aid Application. 100% of need met once admitted.

institutions.name: Colgate University
institutions.scholarship: Meets full demonstrated need; no-loan policy for all admitted students
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 15 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans in aid packages; Colgate meets 100% of demonstrated financial need.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for all applicants (both US and international). Aid must be applied for before admission decision. No loans in international aid packages. Full need met once admitted.

institutions.name: Colorado College
institutions.scholarship: Meets full demonstrated need; no-loan aid packages
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision I · January 15 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Unique Block Plan (one course at a time). No loans in aid packages. Meets full demonstrated need.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for internationals. Strong aid available for those with high financial need.

institutions.name: Columbia University
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need once admitted, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 1 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans. Columbia meets 100% of demonstrated need for all admitted students. However, Columbia is need-aware for international applicants — aid status is one factor in admission.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. International students admitted without requesting aid cannot apply for aid later. Once admitted with aid, 100% of need is met.

institutions.name: Cornell University
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need once admitted
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 2 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Cornell meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted international students. Aid packages include Cornell grants, annual work-study, and reasonable student loans. Need-blind for US domestic students only.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. CSS Profile required for all internationals seeking aid. Aid packages for internationals include loans.

institutions.name: Dartmouth College
institutions.scholarship: Need-blind for all; meets 100% of demonstrated need, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 2 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans. Dartmouth meets 100% of demonstrated need for all admitted students including internationals (need-blind for internationals). Zero parent contribution for families ≤$65K; full-tuition scholarship for families ≤$125K.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind for all applicants including internationals.

institutions.name: Davidson College
institutions.scholarship: Davidson Trust — need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of need with no loans once admitted
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 15 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Davidson Trust: meets 100% of demonstrated need with no loans for all admitted students. However, need-aware for non-US applicants — financial need is considered during admission. Aid limited to first-year students who have not previously enrolled elsewhere.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. Aid must be requested at time of application. 100% of need met with no loans once admitted.

institutions.name: Duke University
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of demonstrated need once admitted, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 2 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: ~$60,000 average grant; Karsh International Scholars: separate merit full-ride
coverage.notes: No loans. Duke meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted international students. Need-aware for internationals — financial need considered in admission. Also offers Karsh International Scholars: competitive full merit scholarship for top international students (separate application).

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. Must declare interest in aid on original application. Karsh International Scholars program available as a separate merit application.

institutions.name: Georgetown University
institutions.scholarship: Meets full demonstrated need; no-loan packages for qualifying students
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Action · January 10 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Georgetown is technically need-blind in admissions for all applicants, but institutional aid funding for internationals is extremely limited. If not awarded aid in the first year, not eligible in subsequent years. CSS Profile required by February 1.

eligibility.notes: Need-blind in admissions (all applicants reviewed without considering finances), but international aid funding is very limited. Must indicate financial aid interest on original application.

institutions.name: Grinnell College
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets 100% of need once admitted, no loans
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 15 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: No loans. Grinnell meets 100% of demonstrated need for all admitted students. One of the most generous small colleges. Need-aware for international applicants.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants — need-blind policy applies to US citizens/eligible noncitizens only. CSS Profile or Grinnell ISAFA required. 100% of need met once admitted.

institutions.name: Hamilton College
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; meets demonstrated need once admitted, may include loans
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 15 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. Hamilton offers strong need-based aid once admitted, but financial need may affect admission for non-US citizens. Aid packages may include loans.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants — need-blind policy applies to US citizens only.

institutions.name: Haverford College
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; need-based aid available but limited for non-US applicants
institutions.deadline: November 15 — Early Decision I · January 15 — Regular Decision

coverage.annualValue: ~$52,000 average grant (for those who receive aid)
coverage.notes: Need-aware for international applicants. Haverford has a smaller endowment than Amherst/Williams and cannot extend need-blind admission to non-US citizens. Aid packages for internationals may include loans.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants — need-blind policy applies to US citizens only.

institutions.name: Johns Hopkins University
institutions.scholarship: Need-aware for internationals; need-based aid available with expanding international commitment
institutions.deadline: November 1 — Early Decision · January 2 — Regular Decision

coverage.notes: JHU is need-blind for US citizens but need-aware for international applicants. Expanding international financial aid from 2026-27 onward. Aid packages may include loans for internationals.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for international applicants — need-blind policy applies to US citizens/eligible noncitizens only.

eligibility.notes: Need-aware for internationals. Strong aid once admitted.
